Because think about it, if now we're using GitHub as the state, right, which is how it should be, every agent here should be able to be restarted because they shouldn't lose context, correct? And I think that's almost the key test, right? If every action, every information, every bit of information is now stored in that GitHub repo, we should be able to move that agent around, and the agent, and in fact, we're going to have multiple collaborating at the same time, which is why it's so important. But also, we should be able to archive those agents that have done a bit of work, and now we don't need it anymore. Because to restart an agent, it should just be a case of starting a new session with the right, with the right repository, isn't it?
decision: GitHub is the state. Every agent commits everything it needs to its own repository, so it can be restarted, moved, or run alongside others without losing context: restarting an agent is a new session with the right repository and its hand-over note. That is the test each agent must pass. Sessions are active only while there is work or feedback from Dinis is needed; otherwise they are handed over and archived (the offboarding process, case 1), so fewer agents run. Agents use the cheapest model that can do their work: Sonnet unless the task needs Opus.
actions: maestro.b, with accountant.b, proposes an activity timeline per agent and a model per role, and runs the restart test on a few agents first; each maestro then applies it on its account. Model changes and restarts with new start prompts are made through mandates from decisions.b.
